companies.name: Y Combinator

companies.name: Discord
companies.context: In early talks with bankers about an IPO potentially coming as soon as 2025; founded from a failed mobile game studio, now profitable with massive community user base including a 15M-member Midjourney server.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.context: Launched Alexa Plus, a generative AI-powered voice assistant at $20/month (free for Prime members), capable of multi-step agentic tasks like ordering groceries, controlling smart home devices, and booking services.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.context: CEO Dario Amodei's blog post 'Machines of Loving Grace' predicts powerful AI systems matching Nobel Prize-level intellect emerging in late 2026 to early 2027; Claude 3.7 Sonnet launch drove significant new spending volume on Ramp.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.context: Tops Ramp's list of new SaaS customers by new customer count; meme post suggested OpenAI could offer a $1M/month AGI subscription plan; 19% of US businesses have adopted OpenAI models vs 4.7% for Anthropic.

companies.name: Apple
companies.context: Siri AI overhaul facing engineering problems and software bugs, threatening to postpone features to May or later; new Mac Studio with M4 Max and M3 Ultra announced; Apple Vision Pro discussed as close but not quite achieving product-market fit.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.context: Mentioned in context of Italy souring on Starlink deal; Tesla sales in Europe dropping and shares in China down 49% amid concerns about Elon Musk's proximity to the Trump administration.

companies.name: Starlink
companies.context: Italy reportedly souring on a $1.6B deal with Starlink amid concerns about US pulling back from European security commitments and Musk's Trump ties; FAA may switch from Verizon to Starlink.

companies.name: Rainmaker
companies.context: Augustus Doricko's weather modification company uses drones and silver iodide to seed clouds for rain and snow; transitioning from barracks-style factory living to more professional operations; active in the Western US and Middle East.

companies.name: Regent Craft
companies.context: Billy Thalheimer's company launched the world's first sea glider prototype — a 65-foot wingspan, 15,000-pound all-electric wing-in-ground-effect vehicle regulated as a boat; 100 employees, breaking ground on 255,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in Rhode Island, targeting entry to service in late 2026 to early 2027.

companies.name: Wischoff Ventures
companies.context: Nicole Wischoff's solo GP fund focused on pre-seed/seed stage companies in unsexy verticals; raised $5M Fund I in 2021, $20M Fund II in 2022, $50M Fund III in 2024; ~$80M AUM.

companies.name: Kratos AI
companies.context: Nicole Wischoff co-founded this next-gen AI data center company targeting 10-25 megawatt facilities near tier 2/3 cities for inference workloads; first facility is 20 megawatts at ~$100M build cost, structured as ~75% debt / 25% equity.

companies.name: Scale AI
companies.context: Alexander Wang cited US companies making up 74% of global market cap and S&P returns of 297% since 2008 vs. rest of world at -4%.

companies.name: Ramp

companies.name: Flock Safety

topics.name: Vibe Coding and LLM-Generated Code
topics.summary: Garry Tan revealed that 95% of code in YC's Winter 2025 batch is LLM-generated; argued that technical founders using AI have a major advantage and those not using it are 'leaving time and attention on the table'; pushed back on anti-vibe-coding sentiment as 'cope'.

topics.name: Discord IPO
topics.summary: Discord is in early talks with bankers about an IPO potentially this year; hosts provided deep history of Jason Citron's founder journey from OpenFeint to Hammer and Chisel to Discord; discussed valuation complexity of network vs. SaaS businesses and compared to Reddit's $40B cap on losses.

topics.name: Amazon Alexa Plus Launch
topics.summary: Amazon launched Alexa Plus with generative AI agentic capabilities for $20/month or free with Prime; Ben Thompson criticized the lack of event video as potentially vaporware but a hands-on confirmed it works; analysts argued Amazon and Apple should be more conservative and focus on ecosystem advantages rather than overpromising.

topics.name: Anthropic AGI Timeline Prediction
topics.summary: Dario Amodei's 'Machines of Loving Grace' blog predicts powerful AI matching Nobel Prize-level intellect emerging in late 2026 to early 2027 with autonomous reasoning, physical world control, and extended task execution; hosts discussed optimistically but noted physical world constraints like energy and manufacturing remain bottlenecks.

topics.name: YC Hard Tech and Defense Tech Renaissance
topics.summary: Garry Tan pushed back on critics wanting YC to 'stick with SaaS'; highlighted YC companies in satellites (Albedo, Astrnis), nuclear (Oklo, Helium), defense, and weather modification; argued 90% AI and growing hard tech portfolio reflects the full opportunity space.

topics.name: Rainmaking and Weather Modification
topics.summary: Augustus Doricko detailed Rainmaker's drone-based cloud seeding technology using silver iodide; discussed political challenges of weather modification regulation (Tennessee trying to criminalize it), ambitious targets like restoring the Great Salt Lake, and long-term terraforming vision.

topics.name: Sea Gliders and Maritime Electric Aviation
topics.summary: Billy Thalheimer announced the first sea glider prototype hitting the water; explained the regulatory arbitrage of operating under Coast Guard maritime jurisdiction, the aerodynamic efficiency of ground-effect flight, hydrofoil wave tolerance, and blown-wing low-speed takeoff enabling a new regional transportation mode.

topics.name: Founder Mode and Zero-Based Leadership
topics.summary: Garry Tan discussed applying founder mode at YC, inspired by Brian Chesky's Airbnb turnaround story; argues zero-based accounting and first-principles thinking are essential for any leader, drawing parallels to DOGE-style government efficiency efforts.

topics.name: DTC and E-Commerce Evolution
topics.summary: Connor McDonald's post on DTC brands navigating deteriorating ad channels prompted discussion of the Facebook ads boom, rising CAC, and shift to omnichannel retail; hosts discussed how brands like Ridge that stayed scientific about performance marketing are surviving while others have struggled.

topics.name: American Manufacturing and Reindustrialization
topics.summary: Multiple guests and posts discussed the need for dramatically more American manufacturing capacity; Garry Tan cited Balaji on the US needing 1000x more manufacturing; Augustus discussed supply chain nationalism and buying American or Taiwanese components; Alexander Wang data highlighted US market cap dominance.

topics.name: Siri Engineering Struggles
topics.summary: Bloomberg reported Apple's long-promised AI Siri overhaul is facing engineering problems and software bugs, with some features delayed to May or later; Ben Thompson argued Apple should leverage its ecosystem advantage rather than overpromising.

topics.name: Italy Souring on Starlink Deal
topics.summary: Italy reportedly having doubts about completing a $1.6B Starlink deal amid concerns about US pulling back from European security commitments and Elon Musk's closeness to the Trump administration; Tesla sales also declining in Europe.

topics.name: AI Biological Computing
topics.summary: Cortical Labs launched the first commercial biological computer with human neurons integrated into silicon chips, described as programmable, adaptive living computation with inherent advantages in energy efficiency (~30W), self-organization, and flexibility.

topics.name: Kangaroo Market
topics.summary: Hosts discussed the 'kangaroo market' meme describing current volatile markets that bounce up and down; framed it optimistically as always having bull markets somewhere even in turbulent periods.

topics.name: AI Data Centers and Inference Infrastructure
topics.summary: Nicole Wischoff announced Kratos AI to build 10-25 megawatt data centers near tier 2/3 cities for AI inference workloads, arguing hyperscalers won't own all inference and there's a large market for smaller co-location facilities; structured as 75% debt / 25% equity.

topics.name: Gundo Hard Tech Ecosystem
topics.summary: Augustus Doricko provided an update on the El Segundo hard tech cluster; noted a new younger cohort (ages 19-23) of companies including subsea vehicle builders; discussed supply chain nationalism, Rangeview foundry as shared supplier, and making hard tech aesthetically cool to attract talent away from finance and software.

topics.name: Flock Safety Series D
topics.summary: Flock Safety raising at $7.5B valuation per Katie Roof scoop; described as the 'Palantir of local governments' selling cameras and equipment to police departments with high switching costs and sticky cohorts.

topics.name: Nuclear Fission Excitement
topics.summary: Augustus Doricko cited nuclear fission as the area of hard tech he is most excited about beyond his own company; praised Isaiah Taylor's Valor Atomics for Ward Zero aesthetics and technical progress, with Ward 1 coming online in the Philippines.
